html:
A railway of about 700 km opened in 1963 to carry iron ore from the mines at Zouerat in the northern desert to the port of Nouadhibou on the Atlantic.

The French-led company MIFERMA built it, and the state took it over in 1974. Its ore trains, often more than two kilometres long, are among the longest and heaviest in the world, and poor travellers ride on top of the ore for free. Iron ore became the main export of Mauritania. The Polisario Front attacked the line during the Western Sahara War. Part of it runs along the edge of Western Sahara.
sum: A railway of about 700 km opened in 1963 to carry iron ore from the mines at Zouerat in the northern desert to the port of Nouadhibou on the Atlantic.
